This petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of M.V.Act, 1989 claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- in respect of accidental injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic Accident.
2 . I n t h e p e t i t i o n i t i s s t a t e d t h a t o n 2 9 .
0 4 . 2 0 2 3 p e t i t i o n e r w a s g o i n g o n Ramachandrapuram-Tirupathi road
by riding a motor cycle bearing reg.No.AP-03-CX-4665 along with his relative Khader Valli as pillion rider slowly and cautiously on the left side of the road and both were wearing helmets.

When they reached near Ambedkar colony, Tirpathi Rural Mandal, one car bearing reg.No.KA-03-NB-5977 came from same direction a high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's vehicle to its rear side and caused accident.
Due to the impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident petitioner was shifted to Ruya hospital, Tirupati and after first aid he was referred to CMC hospital, Vellore and found that Petitioner sustained left talus open fracture and left ankle dislocation.
He took treatment as inpatient from 30.04.2023 to 06.05.2023.
He was treated in the form of ORIF with screws, debridement for ankle, ankle spanning, external fixation application and also took treatment as outpatient.
Petitioner is physically and functionally disabled.
He spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical treatment and other expenses.
3. It is further stated in the petition that prior to accident, petitioner was Mason by profession and he was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
After the accident, till filing of this case petitioner was completely bedridden and lost his earnings.
In future petitioner cannot do mason work to earn his livelihood due to disability.
The accident caused purely due to the rash and negligent driving of car bearing reg.No.KA-03-NB-5977 by its driver.
The jurisdictional Tirchanur Police have registered case in Crime No.132/2023 against the said driver of the car for the offence p/u/s 337 of IPC.
1 st respondent is R.C owner and 2nd respondent is insurance company therefore, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
On all these grounds he prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- in the above case.
4. On issuance of notice, respondent no.1 is served, but he remained absent and therefore he is placed exparte.

2 nd respondent appeared through his counsel and filed written statement contending that this respondent is the insurer of Car bearing reg.No.KA-03-NB-5977 and liability to indemnify the 1 st respondent is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy, provisions of MV Act valid and effective driving license held by the driver of the car, valid R.C and also subject to confirmation of Section 64VB of Insurance Act.
Protection u/s 147 and 149(2) of M.V.Act is sought.
Compliance of Sec. 134 (c) and 158 of Motor Vehicle Act is disputed.
Further he contended that the alleged accident took place on 29.04.2023.
However complaint lodged on 01.05.2023 after lapse of 2 days from the date of alleged accident, therefore car is falsely implicated in the case.
No valid reasons assigned for the delay in lodging the complaint.
That this claim petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties i.e, rider and owner of the motor cycle.
Further the rider of the motor cycle did not possess valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
Owner of the vehicle committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
The medical treatment and expenses alleged by the petitioner are denied.
The age, occupation, income and permanent disability alleged by the petitioner all are denied.
In the event if this Hon'ble court awards compensation the rate of interest shall not exceed 6% in view of law declared by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
On all these grounds it prayed to dismiss the claim petition.

On the basis of above pleadings, this tribunal has framed following:-
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 29.04.2023 at about 6.30 pm when he reached near Ambedkhar colony, Tirupati Rural, Tirupati District on two wheeler bearing reg.No.AP-03-CX-4665 taking one Khadar Valli as pillion rider slowly and cautiously by observing traffic rules, one Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-NB-5977 came from same direction in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the two wheeler and caused accident due to which petitioner sustained grievous injuries as alleged?
2.
Whether the petitioner proves his age, occupation, income and permanent disability if any?
3. Whether the R-2 proves driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-NB-5977 had no effective D.L as on the date of accident as alleged?
4. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so by whom and what is the quantum?
5 . What Order or Award?

[
6. To prove his case, petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1.
Through him Ex.P.1 to P.11 documents are marked.
Doctor by name S.A.Somashekara is examined as P.W.2 and through him Ex.P.12 to 13 documents are marked.
On the contrary, MRO of SVRRGG hospital, Tirupati is examined as R.W.1.
Through him Ex.R.1 to R-5 documents are marked and respondent side evidence is closed.

7. Heard learned counsel for both sides and perused records.
8.

On taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Tribunal and on hearing arguments, my answers to the above issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.3: In the Negative,
Issue No.4: Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.5: As per final order, for the following;
REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1: To prove the petition averments petitioner entered into witness box and got examined as P.W.1.
In his chief examination he reiterated the petition averments and contended that the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-NB-5977 was negligent in driving the vehicle.

To prove this fact he has produced FIR, first information, accident information report, rough sketch, wound Sardar Valli .S vs Saadi Saiteja on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43918976/
3 certificate, final report along with discharge summary.

They show that, father of the petitioner herein by name Noor Ahmed has given first information to Thirachunur police stating that his elder son Khader Valli and second son Sardar Valli were going on two wheeler No. AP-03- CX-4655 and when they reached near Ambedkar Colony, Tirupathi road, Ramachandrapuram, one Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-NB-5977 came in rash and negligent manner and hit the two wheeler from behind.
That, his younger son Sardar Valli sustained injuries to his left leg joint and Khader Valli sustained simple injuries.
That they were taken to nearby Ruya hospital by ambulance and Sardar Valli was referred for higher treatment to CMC hospital.
This fact was informed to this first informant by his elder son Khader Valli and this first informant went to CMC hospital to see his son.
Later on the next day on 01.05.2023 this first informant went to police station and fave first information about the accident and requested the police to take action.
Ont he basis of the said first information Thiruchunur police have registered Crime No.132/2023 against the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-NB-5977 for the offence p/u/s 337 of IPC.
On the same day sketch is prepared which shows accident took place on the left side of road towards Tirupathi.
In the wound certificate of CMC hospital it is mentioned that petitioner was found in casualty on 30.04.2023 with the history of RTA on 29.04.2023.
Charge sheet is filed against the driver of the car stating that he was negligent in driving the vehicle and escaped from the spot due to fear of public.
In the discharge summary dated 06.05.2023 it is mentioned that patient by name Sardar Valli was admitted to hospital with the alleged history of RTA 4 wheeler V/s 2 wheeler.
10. In the cross examination of P.W.1 he denied having no D.L of the petitioner at the time of accident.
He denied that two wheeler had no insurance.
He admitted that there is delay of 3 days in giving first information.
He stated that since he went to hospital and his family was in the hospital there is delay in filing the complaint.
He further admitted that his father has given first information and he had not seen the accident.
He denied that he knows the driver of the car and in collussion with driver, owner and police, false complaint is filed against the car driver.
He denied car was not involved in the accident and stated that he has mentioned in the hospital as to how he sustained injuries.

11. Now it is necessary to notice that, rash and negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-NB-5977 has been supported by FIR and final report coupled with wound certificate and discharge summary showing history of RTA.
These documents are not challenged by the owner or the driver of the car.
In the present case, owner has been placed exparte and not contested the case of petitioner.
Though insurance company disputed the claim, has not given any evidence to prove the averments made in the written statement.

One R.W.1 who is MRO of SVRRGG hospital,
Tirupathi has produced MLC extract at Ex.R.3 which also supports the case of petitioner though R.W.1 is summoned through respondent side.
In Ex.R.3 it is mentioned that, RTA between bike V/s car on 29.04.2023 and S.Sardar Valli sustained injuries.

All these documents and oral evidence show that the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA- 03-NB-5977 was negligent in driving the vehicle and there is no contrary evidence to dispute or to disprove the same.
Therefore in the opinion of this court petitioner has proved negligence on the part of driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-NB-5977.
Hence, I hold Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

4 12. ISSUE NO.2 :
In respect of age, petitioner produced his aadhaar card at Ex.P.9 which shows that he was born on 19.11.1993.
Accident took place on 29.04.2023.
In discharge summary his age is shown as 29 years.
Respondent no.2 disputed the age of the petitioner.
But no satisfactory material is produced to dispute the age.
He was aged 29 years at the time of accident.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner is considered as 29 years at the time of accident.
13. In respect of occupation it is stated that, petitioner was doing Mason work and he was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
To prove this fact he has not produced any documents.
Therefore notional income has to be considered.
Accident took place in 2023.

Hence, considering the cost of living and petitioner being resident of Chittor District, Andhra pradesh his monthly income is considered Rs.
16,000/- per month.
14. In respect of permanent disability a doctor by name S.A.Somashekara-Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria hospital is examined as P.W.2.
In his chief examination he stated that he examined petitioner on 21.10.2024 and petitioner mentioned before doctor that he met with accident on 29.04.2023.

As per the examination of P.W.2 doctor, petitioner walks with pain and limping,
wasting of left lower limb is seen.
Surgical and secondary scars are seen over left ankle.
Fractures united.
Implants in situ and according to doctor disability in the left lower limb is 42% and whole body impairment is 21%.

In his cross examination, 2nd respondent disputed assessment made by the doctor and contended that exaggerated assessment of disability is done by the doctor without examining all the reports and without consulting treated doctor.
It is necessary to notice that doctor can state about the physical disability and not the functional disability.

In the present case,
petitioner is said to be Mason.

The physical disability in left lower limb will come in the way of mason work and he may not be able to do the mason work to the satisfaction of his employer due to the disability in the left lower limb.
Consequently it may affect the income of the petitioner.

Further,
petitioner being still young in his 30's, can come out of the disability in his future.
Therefore, in the opinion of this court there is functional disability affecting the income of the petitioner at 10%.
Accordingly, I answer this issue Partly in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.3 :
Respondent no.2 contended that driver of the aforesaid car was not holding valid driving licenc as on the date of accident.
But to prove this fact no evidence is led by 2 nd respondent.
Therefore, the said contention in the written statement is not proved by evidence of 2 nd respondent.
Hence, I answer this issue in the "Negative".
16. ISSUE NO.4 :
In view of above reasons, injuries sustained by petitioner are due to the accident caused by the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-NB-5977.
There is nexus between the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the accident.
Hence he is entitled to compensation at the hands of respondents.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under:
(I) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.10 and 11.
Totally he has paid amount of Rs.90,767/- as per Ex.P.11 medical bills.
The said payment of bill is due to the accident caused to him.
They are subsequent to the date of accident.
Though they are disputed, no satisfactory material is placed to disbelieve the bills.
They are supported by prescriptions of the doctor.

Therefore, petitioner is Sardar Valli .S vs Saadi Saiteja on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43918976/
5 entitled for medical expenses of Rs.90,767/-.

sentences.text: (ii) Food and nourishment:
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.7 discharge summary of Christian Medical College Vellore hospital.
It shows that he was admitted on 30.04.2023 and discharged on 06.05.2023.
He was in hospital for 7 days.
Accident took place in the year 2023.
Since he was in hospital, food and nourishment charges will have to be awarded.
Considering the cost of living, and food, nourishment charges if per day Rs.500/- is awarded it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence for food and nourishment Rs.500/- x 07 days = Rs. 3,500/- is awarded.
(iii) Attendant charges:
For a period of inpatient for 07 days some one should have looked after petitioner in the hospital.
Even if his family member has taken care of him in the said period, that family member's income for those days is lost.
Hence per day if Rs.500/- is awarded as attendant charges in 2023, it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence for attendant charges Rs.500/- x 07 days =Rs.3,500/-is awarded.
(iv) Loss of income during laid up period:
As per the finding to issue No.2, the income of the petitioner per month is Rs.16,000/-.
He suffered grievous injuries.
He was inpatient for 07 days and he was advised to take rest.
Minimum 3 months is required to recover from such grievous injury.

Therefore, laid up period of petitioner is considered as total 3 months including in patient period and loss of income during laid up period is Rs.16,000/-x 3= 48,000/- He is entitled to Rs.48,000/-
as loss of income during laid up period.
(v) Conveyance charges:
It is stated that petitioner took treatment in CMC hospital, Vellore.
He has spent money for conveyance for the purpose of treatment.
Considering the same, this court is of the opinion that amount of Rs.3,000/- shall be awarded as conveyance charges.
(vi) Loss of future income due to Disability :
As per the findings given to issue no.2, there is functional disability of 10%.
Therefore, loss of future income due to disability is to be calculated as income per month Rs.16,000 X 12 months X 10% disability X appropriate multiplier to the age group of 26-30 is 17.
Hence, in the opinion of this court, petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.3,26,400/- towards loss of future income due to disability.
(vii) For Future medical expenses: P.W.2 has not stated anything about the need of further treatment to the petitioner.
There is no evidence to show that the petitioner needs further medical treatment.
Therefore no compensation is awarded under this head.
(viii) For Pain and sufferings:
The petitioner has sustained one grievous injury.
The records show that he underwent treatment and operation.
He was in hospital for 07 days and suffered pain and agony.
Therefore, for pain and suffering the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- .

Sardar Valli .S vs Saadi Saiteja on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43918976/
6 (ix) Physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life :

sentences.text:
As per the evidence of assessed doctor,
petitioner complained about pain and difficulty.
He underwent operation and suffers discomfort.
Meaning, he cannot lead the normal life as he used to live before the accident.
Certainly accident has caused physical discomfort and came in the way of normal enjoyment of life of petitioner.
Hence in the opinion of this court, petitioner is entitled to compensation under the head of physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life.

Under the said head he is entitled for Rs.30,000/-
(x) Loss of future prospect:

As per the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme court, even in injury cases,
loss of future prospect has to be considered.
But in the present case, the on going through the evidence of assessed doctor and the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner there is no chance of loss of future prospect.
Hence no compensation is awarded under this head.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:-

Therefore, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.5,35,167/- in respect of injuries sustained by him in the Road traffic accident.
Accordingly, I answer this Issue "Partly in Affirmative".
17. ISSUE NO.5:-
In view of above reasons petitioner is entitled to compensation from the hands of Respondents.

Since 2nd respondent admitted the insurance policy valid as on the date of accident,
he is liable to indemnify the insured and pay compensation to the petitioner to the tune of Sardar Valli .S vs Saadi Saiteja on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43918976/
7 Rs.5,35,167/-with interest @ of 6% from the date of petition till the date of payment.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass following :
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,35,167/- with interest @ 6% pa on the said amount from the date of petition till the date of payment.
The respondent no.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured and directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest within one month from the date of this order.
On such deposit, the petitioner is entitled to have release of 50% of the compensation and remaining 50% shall be kept in F.D for a period of 3 years with liberty to draw periodical interest.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.

It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,35,167/- with interest @ 6% pa on the said amount from the date of petition till the date of payment.
The respondent no.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured and directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest within one month from the date of this order.
On such deposit, the petitioner is entitled to have release of 50% of the compensation and remaining 50% shall be kept in F.D for a period of 3 years with liberty to draw periodical interest.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.
